body.objective: Students will be able to draw in two-point perspective.
body.iCan: I can draw in two-point perspective.
successCriteria: I can draw objects in two-point perspective
I can place a horizon line and vanishing points
I can use perspective to show depth in a scene
body.hook: Stand at the end of a long hallway and the walls, floor and ceiling all seem to rush toward a single point. Renaissance artists worked out the rules for this effect over 500 years ago, and those rules still power architecture drawings, video game levels and film storyboards today.

vocabulary.definition: A system for showing three-dimensional space on a flat surface.
A horizontal line at the viewer's eye level.
A point on the horizon line where parallel lines appear to meet.
A system with two vanishing points, used when an object is viewed from a corner.
Lines that go toward a vanishing point.
The height from which the viewer sees the scene.

study.title: Corner Views
study.question: How do artists create convincing space with two-point perspective?
study.passage:
Step 1: Draw a horizon line across the page. Place two vanishing points (VP1 and VP2) far apart on it, near the edges of the page.
Step 2: Draw a vertical line for the nearest corner of a box.
Step 3: From the top and bottom of that line, draw light lines to both vanishing points.
Step 4: Draw two more vertical lines to set the width of each side.
Step 5: From the tops of those lines, draw lines to the opposite vanishing points; where they cross is the back corner of the top.
Step 6: Erase guidelines and add value: one side light, one side medium, the top lightest.
Eye level: If the box is above the horizon line, you see its bottom. If it's below, you see its top. If the horizon line passes through it, you see neither.
Challenge (25 minutes): Draw a street corner with at least three buildings, a sidewalk and windows, all in two-point perspective. Add one figure or object for scale.
Real-world link: architects, interior designers, game level designers and storyboard artists all use perspective drawing.

examples.title: Vanishing points
examples.problem: Why place vanishing points far apart?
examples.answer: Far-apart points make shapes look natural, not stretched
examples.explore: What happens if they're too close?

examples.title: Windows
examples.problem: How do you make windows follow perspective?
steps: Draw their top and bottom edges toward the vanishing point
examples.answer: Use guidelines from the vanishing point for each row
examples.explore: Why do windows look smaller farther away?

examples.title: Value
examples.problem: How can value make a box look solid?
examples.answer: Light top, medium side, darker side

items.q: Define vanishing point.
items.answer: A point on the horizon line where parallel lines appear to meet.

items.q: What is the horizon line?
items.answer: A horizontal line at the viewer's eye level.

items.q: Describe the steps to draw a box in two-point perspective.
items.answer: Horizon and two VPs, nearest vertical edge, lines to both VPs, side verticals, connect to opposite VPs.

items.q: Explain what you see when a box is above, on and below the horizon.
items.answer: Above: bottom; on: neither; below: top.

items.q: Why add value to perspective drawings?
items.answer: To make forms look solid and show light direction.

items.answer: Low eye level makes subjects feel large; high makes them feel small.
